newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey lost $60 billion in Iraq embargo - minister. [CORRECTED 21:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Turkey lost $60 billion in Iraq embargo - minister. [CORRECTED 21:20 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects figure in headline to "$60 billion" from "$60 million")
A Turkish cabinet member said on Sunday that Turkey had so far lost $60 billion from the six-year-old U.N. embargo on Iraq, Anatolian news agency said.
Turkish officials have previously put the loss, from trade with neighbour Baghdad and cheap oil imports, at around $27 billion. Western diplomats say even that figure is probably too high.
"The loss so far is $60 billion," the semi-official Anatolian agency quoted State Minister Ahmet Cemil Tunc as telling a news conference before he left on a trip to Iraq.
"Turkey has suffered as much from this embargo as the Iraqi people have," he said.
Tunc is to meet President Saddam Hussein, Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf, Trade Minister Mohammed Mehdi Saleh and several other officials during his visit, until April 4.
"The target of the visit is to develop trade relations between Turkey and Iraq and bring them to the level they were at before the war. There is the will for that on both sides," he said.
Iraq was Turkey's third-largest trading partner before U.N. sanctions were slapped on Baghdad for invading Kuwait in 1990.
Last week some Turkish companies began selling pulses and vegetable oil to Iraq as the first shipments of food items under a U.N. oil-for-food deal.
